Eddy McNally had by far his best run ever and will in the weeks ahead be a force to be reckoned with. Les Harris also showed us he can turn in a good one.
BEAUFOY---Les Harris won the school mile in 5:04.2 but has a superior 1500 metres clocking of 4:29.7 to his credit. He was also this year's winner of the A.T.C. mile (4:56).
(l.to r.) Bill Curtin, Peter Carton, John Stow and Les Harris

Les Harris was an excellent 4th in this race. Lee Sullivan shared the same time (11.5) as the first and second when being placed third in the Junior 100 metres in a S.C.A.A.A. open meeting at Crystal Palace on Oct 15th.

Les Harris had one of his best runs to date to finish second on the opening stage, just eight seconds in arrears, but Vic Butcher was not at his best and had the misfortune to face Adams of West Surrey who raced away to record second fastest time of the day.

Peter's efforts have induced others to follow suit and climb to the standards set by Bill Curtin, so instead of having a solitary spearhead and a group of supporting runners down the field we now have Curtin, Carton and John Stow with little separating them and Tony Binda and Les Harris determined to close that gap.
